subject.title: Feature: Per-spawn tool restrictions for sub-agents

question: Should OpenClaw accept an additive per-spawn `sessions_spawn` tool restriction contract now, and should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78441's allow-only `toolsAllow` shape be the V1 API?
rationale: This changes the public spawn API and the enforced child-agent security boundary, so code inspection can verify the gap but cannot choose the long-term product/security contract.

options.title: Accept `toolsAllow` V1
options.body: Use the open PR's allow-only shape as the first supported contract after maintainer review of persistence, unsupported-runtime behavior, docs, and tests.

options.title: Revise to allow/deny policy
options.body: Pause the candidate PR and require an object policy such as `tools: { allow, deny }` if maintainers want deny semantics in the first public API.

options.title: Park the feature
options.body: Keep the issue open as a product/security tracker but do not merge a per-spawn tool API until the subagent policy model is redesigned.

recommendation.title: Accept `toolsAllow` V1
recommendation.body: Use the open PR's allow-only shape as the first supported contract after maintainer review of persistence, unsupported-runtime behavior, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: `steipete` introduced `sessions_spawn` and has recent routing history in the same spawn surface, making him the best available owner for the API/security-boundary choice.
